mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day horizon are not statistically different from a pre-trend period (p > 0.05) or the 60-day average return is positive despite the rate increase.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >2% in a month while UNRATE decreases by >0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or flat despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger condition (p > 0.05 in a two-sample test).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) above 0.3% for two consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which anticipates higher corporate profits and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.3% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative or the 5-day average return is below the 30-day prior average (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% in a month coincides with a decline in inventory levels (not directly observable but implied by supply chain stress), reducing future supply absorption capacity and pushing S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from a neutral baseline (median 0) during supply shocks (p > 0.1).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS crosses above 5%, it indicates a shift toward restrictive policy, which raises real discount rates and dampens equity price expectations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive or the 60-day IC is above 0.05 (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for 4 consecutive months, accompanied by rising labor force participation (HOUST), suggests a tight labor market that drives wage growth and boosts equity valuations, yielding positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for 4 months and HOUST increases by >0.5% in the same period
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) despite the trigger being met.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in retail sales (not directly observable but proxyable via a demand-related series like GDPC1) followed by two months of elevated consumer spending (CPIAUCSL > 2% MoM) predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days as market anticipates sustained growth.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >2% in the month following a >1% one-time spike in GDPC1
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the demand spike (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle regime (regime_hint), a combination of rising inflation (CPIAUCSL) and declining industrial production (INDPRO) creates conflicting expectations that produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL increases by >0.5% while INDPRO falls by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive or the interaction term (CPIAUCSL - INDPRO) is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) within the tightening cycle window.
